neet_che_u03_t04_1.working: Fluorine has the highest Pauling electronegativity, about 4.0. It is higher than O (3.44), Cl (3.16) and N (3.04).

neet_che_u03_t04_2.working: Pauling relation (kcal/mol): Δ = 23(Δχ)². So (Δχ)² = 25/23 = 1.087, giving Δχ ≈ 1.04.

neet_che_u03_t04_3.working: Carbon is sp in ethyne (50% s), sp2 in ethene (33%) and sp3 in ethane (25%). More s-character makes carbon more electronegative, so ethyne > ethene > ethane.

neet_che_u03_t04_4.working: A is false: the energy released on adding an electron to an isolated gaseous atom is electron gain enthalpy, not electronegativity. R is true: electronegativity is a relative, unitless property of a bonded atom.

neet_che_u03_t04_5.working: Statement I is incorrect: oxygen is second, but its Pauling value is about 3.44–3.5, not 3.0. Statement II is incorrect: Δχ for C–H is about 0.35, while for H–Cl it is about 0.96, so H–Cl is more polar.
